Craig Anderton · Polyphony

Pulse Width Multiplier

Voltage-controlled digital audio circuit

← Back to DIY Audio & Video Projects

Description

Four comparator pulse streams are combined through exclusive-OR logic. A triangle input becomes a moving group of pulse widths, producing changing harmonic content and, at some settings, additional pulses per cycle.

Open original source PDF ↗

Materials

Source-checked inventory

The linked archive PDF contains only printed p. 12: text and BOM, but no schematic. The missing circuit drawing has been recovered from the same original article reproduced by mu:zines, Polyphony Jan/Feb 1981, pp. 12–13, and is embedded below. Fixed resistors: ¼ W, preferably 5%. Use the original 4136 pinout for the connections given here. source PDF p. 1.

Reference Quantity Value / specification
R1, R2 2 10 Ω, ¼ W
R3 1 33 kΩ
R4 1 47 kΩ
R5, R6 2 50 kΩ trimmers
R7–R28 22 100 kΩ
R29, R30 2 220 kΩ
Ra 1 Adjustable feedback resistance; choose range below
Rb 1 Fixed feedback resistance; choose below
C1 1 0.22 µF
C2–C4 3 10 µF electrolytic or tantalum, ≥15 V per source; choose margin above actual rail voltage
D1–D4 4 1N4001; article also permits 1N914/equivalent
IC1, IC2 2 4136 quad op amp
IC3 1 4030 or 4070 CMOS quad XOR
Sockets 3 14-pin for each original IC
Audio and CV connectors As configured One audio input, four audio outputs; up to nine CV inputs (three per summer), all with common 0 V return
Initial pulse-width controls Optional, up to 3 One pot may feed one input of each summer; source gives no pot value or panel wiring specification

Select one signal/CV scaling combination

Audio input Control range Ra trimmer Rb fixed
0.5 V peak-to-peak 0 to +5 V 500 kΩ 680 kΩ
5 V peak-to-peak 0 to +5 V 50 kΩ 68 kΩ
10 V peak-to-peak 0 to +10 V 50 kΩ 68 kΩ
20 V peak-to-peak 0 to +10 V 50 kΩ 33 kΩ

Provide regulated +15 V, 0 V, −15 V, board, enclosure, insulated wiring and a scope plus a triangle-wave source. Four outputs are unattenuated CMOS logic signals; a protected/attenuated monitor interface is additional engineering, not a component hidden in the original BOM. No PCB artwork, supply-current requirement or external output buffer is supplied.

Step-by-step guide

Complete circuit drawing and signal path

  1. Select the scaling row and label every connection.

    Choose Ra/Rb from the inventory before assembly. The triangle signal enters C1/R27; IC2D supplies the common scaled triangle bus. IC2A–C are separate inverting CV summers, and IC1A–D act as comparators. Label four outputs, three banks of three CV inputs, both supply rails and 0 V. The signal inputs do not connect directly to CMOS gates.

  2. Check sockets and the asymmetric power arrangement.

    For the original 4136s, connect IC1/IC2 pin 11 to positive and pin 7 to negative. IC3 pin 14 goes to the positive rail and pin 7 to ground. +15 V passes through R1 (10 Ω) to the positive distribution node, with C3 from that node to 0 V, positive end at the rail. −15 V passes through R2 (10 Ω) to the negative distribution node, with C4 positive end at 0 V. The XOR IC must not see the full +15/−15 V span. These connections are visible in the recovered original schematic.

  3. Build the offset and triangle-scaling stage.

    C1 = 0.22 µF couples audio to R27 = 100 kΩ and the inverting input of IC2D, pin 14. Rb and Ra form its feedback path from output pin 12; strap the Ra wiper as shown. R6 is between ground and R3 = 33 kΩ toward the negative rail; its wiper is filtered by C2 and feeds IC2D non-inverting pin 13 through R26 = 100 kΩ. C2 positive goes to ground because the offset is negative. Check this polarity before fitting the IC.

  4. Build each CV summer independently.

    IC2A uses input resistors R7/R8/R9, feedback R10 and non-inverting pin 2 grounded. IC2B uses R12/R13/R14, feedback R15 and non-inverting pin 5 grounded. IC2C uses R17/R18/R19, feedback R20 and non-inverting pin 9 grounded. All these resistors are 100 kΩ. Outputs are pins 3, 4 and 10 respectively. A positive control voltage therefore produces a negative threshold voltage.

  5. Build the fixed and moving comparator thresholds.

    IC1A receives the triangle bus at pin 2 and its threshold at pin 1 through R28 from R5. R5 sits between ground and R4 = 47 kΩ toward the negative rail. The IC2A threshold reaches IC1B positive pin 5 via R29 = 220 kΩ, while triangle reaches negative pin 6 through R11. IC2B reaches IC1C negative pin 8 through R16, while triangle reaches positive pin 9. IC2C reaches IC1D positive pin 13 through R30 = 220 kΩ, while triangle reaches negative pin 14 through R21. Preserve the deliberately different comparator polarities; do not normalize all four.

  6. Fit the analog-to-logic interface.

    IC1 outputs pins 3, 4, 10 and 12 feed the anodes of D1–D4; the cathodes (banded ends) feed the XOR-input nodes. Each node has its own 100 kΩ pull-down, R22–R25, to 0 V. This prevents the negative op-amp swing from being wired straight into a CMOS input. Do not omit the diodes or pull-downs.

  7. Wire the XOR chain and four outputs.

    IC3A has pin 1 grounded and pin 2 driven by D1; pin 3 is output 1. IC3B combines the same D1 node at pin 6 with D2 at pin 5; pin 4 is output 2. IC3C combines output 2 at pin 8 with D3 at pin 9; pin 10 is output 3. IC3D combines output 3 at pin 12 with D4 at pin 13; pin 11 is output 4. Output 1 is therefore a single pulse stream; succeeding outputs can contain two, three and four pulses per triangle period.

  8. Inspect with power off, then check rails without signal.

    Verify polarity of C2–C4, diode bands and all socket pins. Check continuity from every jack sleeve to 0 V and confirm no shorts between rails. Insert ICs with power disconnected. On first power-up verify distribution rails after R1/R2 and stop if a resistor or IC heats. No current limit is specified by the source, so establish a suitable bench protection limit from the actual parts rather than assuming a published figure.

  9. Calibrate IC2D before injecting CV.

    Feed a triangle at the selected input level. Scope IC2D pin 12 relative to 0 V. Adjust Ra for the control range peak-to-peak, then R6 for its offset: with 0–5 V CV the triangle must run from −5 V to 0 V; with 0–10 V CV it must run from −10 V to 0 V. Recheck gain and offset after each adjustment. Calibration method: source PDF p. 1.

  10. Set the fixed pulse and verify the moving pulses.

    Adjust R5 so IC1A output, or logic output 1, has approximately equal high/low times. The article permits other pulse widths but starts from a square wave. With fixed positive CV applied to one summer at a time, check that its comparator changes duty cycle as the threshold crosses the triangle. Then inspect outputs 2–4 at the same time base. Coincident edges can cancel in XOR logic; not every control setting produces the maximum pulse count. source PDF p. 1

  11. Connect modulation and a safe listening path.

    Start with one slow positive CV and add other LFO/envelope sources gradually. Each summer has three equal-value input resistors; the sum, rather than any one jack alone, controls its comparator. For manual initial width a pot can drive one input per bank, but its value and wiring are not specified. The four gate outputs are not line-level audio jacks: verify their voltage on the scope and provide an appropriate attenuation/DC-blocking interface before an amplifier.

  12. Record tests before closing the case.

    Log the chosen Ra/Rb row, triangle extrema, output-1 duty cycle, the response of each CV bank, and the presence of successively richer pulse patterns. Verify changing one bank affects its own comparator and downstream XOR outputs, not the earlier gate outputs. This is the functional acceptance test; no built hardware is claimed here.

Troubleshooting by node

Symptom Specific check
Triangle never reaches 0 V at the top Check IC2D offset: R3/R6/C2/R26 and C2 polarity; confirm the negative supply.
Triangle height cannot be calibrated Check selected Ra/Rb row, C1/R27 and the actual input peak-to-peak level; Ra is additional to R5/R6, not one of those two trimmers.
One comparator sticks high or low A threshold outside the triangle range can intentionally suppress pulses. Reduce summed CV, then check that comparator polarity and its associated summer.
Comparator toggles but gate node stays low Check diode orientation and the relevant 100 kΩ pull-down for a solder short.
All XOR outputs fail Check IC3 supply +rail/ground and the R1 distribution, not the negative op-amp rail. Confirm the actual CMOS package pinout.
Output 1 works, output 2 does not Check IC3 pins 5/6, D2 and IC2A; output 2 uses the D1 node directly, not a newly invented analog mix.
Later output loses pulses at some settings XOR cancels simultaneous equal logic states. Separate thresholds before treating pulse cancellation as failure.
Audio is excessively loud or clicks at a mixer Stop direct connection; gate outputs have logic-level amplitude and DC. The source supplies no audio output conditioning.

Remaining source gaps

The original archive extract alone is incomplete, but the matching original schematic above supplies the missing power and pin wiring. Still absent are PCB artwork, connector mechanics, a supply design/current rating, initial-width pot values, and an attenuated audio-output stage. The article mentions 741/4558/general-purpose op amps as alternatives; these require repinning and, for single/dual packages, a different device count. No drop-in substitution is asserted. The diagram and this text retain the original 4136 version.
